question: How is pressure calculated?
explanation: Pressure is the amount of force spread over a specific surface area, so the standard formula is force divided by area. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T1#BMP112_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is fluid pressure different from the pressure of a solid object?

options.A: Solids can only push sideways against containers
options.B: Fluids do not possess any mass or weight
options.C: Fluid particles can move and transmit force in every direction
options.D: Solid objects cannot exert downward weight

explanation: Fluid particles flow and bump into things freely, meaning they push against all surrounding surfaces, unlike stationary solids. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T1#BMP112_U3_T1_h1)

question: What two main factors determine the pressure at a certain depth inside a stationary liquid?
explanation: Liquid pressure increases directly with how deep the liquid is and how dense the liquid is. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T1#BMP112_U3_T1_h2)

question: If you place two pressure sensors at the exact same depth in plain water—one in a narrow glass cylinder and the other in a wide basin—what will the sensors read?

options.A: The sensor in the narrow cylinder will read higher
options.B: The sensor in the wide basin will read higher
options.C: Both sensors will read the exact same pressure
options.D: Neither sensor will register any measurable pressure

explanation: Liquid pressure depends on depth and density, not on the total volume or shape of the container. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T1#BMP112_U3_T1_h2)

question: What creates pressure inside a container filled with gas?

options.B: Molecules colliding with the container walls
options.C: Liquid droplets condensing near the bottom
options.D: Gravity pulling molecules downward into a solid mass

explanation: Gas pressure is the physical result of gas molecules bouncing rapidly against whatever surfaces enclose them. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T1#BMP112_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why does air pressure decrease as a person climbs a high mountain?

options.A: Gravity stops working completely at high altitudes
options.B: There is a smaller column of air pressing down from above
options.C: The wind blows all the air molecules sideways
options.D: Gas molecules freeze solid in cold mountain air

explanation: Atmospheric pressure is caused by the weight of air overhead, so going higher means less air remains above you. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T1#BMP112_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the standard unit of measurement for pressure?
explanation: The pascal (Pa) is the official unit for pressure, representing one newton of force per square meter. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T1#BMP112_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which unit is most commonly used in clinical practice to measure blood pressure?
explanation: Standard clinical blood pressure monitors measure pressure relative to a column of mercury, expressed as mmHg. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T1#BMP112_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why must an intravenous fluid bag be hung higher than the patient's insertion site during a drip infusion?

options.A: To keep the infusion pump running without using any electricity
options.B: To prevent air bubbles from forming inside the plastic tubing
options.C: To create hydrostatic pressure that overcomes the patient's blood pressure
options.D: To cool down the fluid before it enters the bloodstream

explanation: Elevating the IV bag uses gravity-driven liquid pressure to push fluid smoothly into the vein against internal blood pressure. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T1#BMP112_U3_T1_h5)

question: If an IV fluid bag is lowered to the same level as the patient's arm instead of being kept elevated on the drip stand, what will most likely happen to the infusion?

options.A: The plastic tubing will instantly burst from high pressure
options.B: The infusion rate will remain completely unchanged
options.C: The fluid will flow much faster into the patient's vein
options.D: Blood will flow backward from the vein into the IV tubing

explanation: Without pressure from elevation, the patient's blood pressure will push blood back up into the IV tubing. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T1#BMP112_U3_T1_h5)
